title: Main gear
object: Fixed main landing gear of a four-seat high-wing light aircraft: a tapered spring-steel leg clamped in the fuselage's gear box, its axle, 6.00-6 wheel and single-disc hydraulic brake, in section on the leg's mid-plane, with the toe-brake master cylinder in section
idea: A steel beam is the spring, and Pascal's principle is the brake: one leg bends to take the landing, one toe stops one wheel
summary: The mains touch down at 1 m/s and each tapered leg bends as a cantilever on its two fittings: from beam theory, 59 mm at the axle under the static 4.48 kN, at about 320 MPa, which spreads the track by 62 mm and swings each wheel's camber from +6.4° in the air to 0° at rest. With no oil damper the steel gives the landing back as a bounce. Then the toes press: the pedal multiplies the toe force 2.5 times, the master cylinder turns it into line pressure p = F/A, the same pressure pushes the caliper's Ø44.45 piston, the disc is clamped from both sides and the torque slows the aeroplane; one toe alone drags one wheel and turns it.
usedFor: Pilot and maintenance training: what spring gear does on landing, why the wheels lean and scrub, how toe brakes, master cylinders and calipers work and what a spongy pedal means
Engineering courses: cantilever beams with a taper, fully stressed design, two-support reactions, Pascal's principle, disc-brake torque
A software-concept explainer: one input fanned out to independent channels (each toe its own wheel), and a spring that stores and returns energy with no damping
